test_title: PYST 48: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 17 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Bharat goes to a shop to purchase a toy train priced at ₹5,000. He is offered 4 discount options by the shopkeeper. Which of these options should he opt for to gain maximum advantage of the discount offered?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Option 1: 44% and 18% ⇒ net = 1 − (0.56 × 0.82) = 54.08%

Option 2: 30% and 30% ⇒ net = 1 − (0.7 × 0.7) = 51%

Option 3: 22%

Option 4: 24% and 25% ⇒ net = 1 − (0.76 × 0.75) = 43%

Highest discount = 54.08%

**∴ Answer = Option 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price of toy = 5000

Four discount options

**Formula used:**

Successive discount = 1 − (1 − d1)(1 − d2)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Option 1: 44% and 18%

⇒ Net discount = 1 − (0.56 × 0.82) = 1 − 0.4592 = 54.08%

⇒ Option 2: 30% and 30%

⇒ Net discount = 1 − (0.7 × 0.7) = 1 − 0.49 = 51%

⇒ Option 3: 22%

⇒ Net discount = 22%

⇒ Option 4: 24% and 25%

⇒ Net discount = 1 − (0.76 × 0.75) = 1 − 0.57 = 43%

⇒ Maximum discount = 54.08%

**∴ The correct answer is Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

Net = 1 − (1 − d1)(1 − d2)

Common Mistake

Do not add percentages directly

Comparison Rule

Higher effective discount ⇒ better option

Key Insight

Convert all options into single % for comparison
